Moreover, research suggests that DKK3 might be a potential biomarker of lymph node involvement that can improve the predictive power of computed tomography (CT) scans.

Studies have shown that the loss of DKK3 expression is more prevalent in advanced gastric cancer patients compared to those with early-stage disease. This aberrant loss has been linked to increased lymph node metastasis, which is a critical factor in determining the prognosis and treatment options for gastric cancer.

While further research is needed to confirm these findings and establish DKK3 as a reliable biomarker, the current evidence suggests that the loss of this protein may be an important predictor of lymph node metastasis preoperatively. Therefore, investigating ways to identify patients with aberrant DKK3 expression could provide valuable insights into the development and progression of gastric cancer.

It's essential to note that while this information is promising, more studies are required to confirm these findings and establish a definitive role for DKK3 in predicting lymph node metastasis preoperatively.
